They either need to start being more polite or find another job as they clearly don’t enjoy working here, after checking the austpost website you are permitted to send goods with a sealed battery in them - never had an issue but they’ll argue that point for minutes rather than listening to the customer who confirmed its okay to do so

Really disappointing experience after spending $30 to post two things (also a rip off in my eyes for postage.

It’s sad that I have to leave negative reviews but management need to deal with this issue as it’s making locals feel upset - clearly not the only one by other reviews left

My experience was some years ago, but I'm finally saying something now. I was referred to Dr Vivian Yang at 19 by my family doctor who suspected I may have endometriosis. Dr Yang seemed great at first, like she was listening and wanted to try the minimally invasive options first and I was ok with that. But every time she just kept trying to throw more pill prescriptions at me, always wanting to put me on Yaz (imagine trying to get a 19 year old to pay $85 for a box of birth control pills and not even be willing to consider alternative brands that do the same thing for a lot less money!) After the first laparoscopic surgery she spoke to me after the surgery whilst in hospital and confirmed I had endometriosis (both my mother and my then-boyfriend were present). A week later at my follow-up, she backtracked and said that she hadn't said that at all. Also, one of my incision sites was never closed properly and it was blamed on my navel being an "extreme innie" and "too deep" to seal up with the skin glue. It still gets gross with pus 10 years later and there's nothing I can do to fix it.

A few years later,  I had more issues and went to my new GP who was happy for me to go back to Dr Yang, since I already had a history with her. I agreed. I had to see Dr Yang multiple times, every time she just kept trying to throw more and more pill prescriptions at me, always wanting to put me on Yaz, even after I told her that I suffered from migraines with aura. I spoke to my GP about my concerns and she requested a copy of my files from Dr Yang's office for her records. Slipped into this file, Dr Yang had written a letter, saying I suffered from nothing more than dysmenorrhea (see; fancy word for bad period pain). My GP had known me for 4 years at this point and knew I had more going on. I pushed and pushed for myself until eventually, in 2021, she agreed to a second surgery. I had to go to a specific womens clinc in Penrith for my ultrasounds. Unfortunately, due to covid restrictions, my then-partner was not allowed inside the ultrasound room with me. The sonographer was really lovely, explained everything she was doing and seeing, let me watch it all on a big screen, had to call the doctor in to look at something and the doctor confirmed there was definitely a mass around my right ovary and that my left ovary was immobile (stuck; same as it had been in my first surgery). The doctor and sonographer both spoke to me about it in depth and repeated it for my partner when I asked. They said they would have the scans and report to Dr Yang within the week. When I next saw Dr Yang, those scans had mysteriously disappeared and I have still never seen a copy of that report. But I told her she had to call them and get the verbal report because I refused to let her charge me $300 for a useless 5 min appt. The doctor from that clinic confirmed what I had said and Dr Yang finally gave me my second surgery, resulting in a diagnosis of adenomyosis (which, incidentally, my mother had been diagnosed with a few years prior).

Once again, post-op she tried to back track and throw more Yaz prescriptions at me. She told me I was crazy, that I couldn't be experiencing the symptoms I had, that it was all in my head and there was nothing more she could do. I'd had enough. At the suggestion of a friend, I went to a new gynocologist. When this doctor requested Dr Yang' send over a copy of my medical files (with my signed consent), she refused. I showed up 3 weeks later to my next appointment and Dr Yang had refused, ignored and then played dumb about the whole scenario. We had to call them, fax a new signed consent form and demand they send my files over immediately - which, thankfully, they did. The new doctor, confirmed that the scans from before the second surgery were never included in the files and when pressed, Dr Yang again played ignorant, saying she'd never received them or any report. My new gyno was shocked at the level of unprofessionalism.

Please avoid this doctor, she is cold, callous, uncaring and unprofessional. Save yourself the headache.

one_star_reviews.text:
Dear Containers for Change Management,

I would like to bring an incident to your attention regarding the service we received at your Crestmead facility on Sunday morning.

My wife and I attended at approximately 7:30am to recycle a quantity of cans and bottles. We don't use the Containers for Change facility very often, although we have used the large hopper-style machine previously where you simply pour the containers in.

On this occasion, some of the bottles we had were already crushed, as they had come from a house clean-up we had been doing. Unfortunately, a number of the bottles became caught in the machine, causing it to block and require several resets.

What concerned us was the behaviour of the young male staff member who was monitoring the machine. His frustration was clearly visible to us on the large screen, including hand gestures being directed towards us. We also had an error come up and pressed the "Call for Staff" button several times, but despite this, the staff member appeared to deliberately ignore the request and did not come over to assist us.

Eventually, the bottles cleared themselves and we were able to continue, but we were quite disappointed with the way the situation was handled — or, more accurately, not handled.

We completely understand that machines can jam and that staff can have frustrating moments, particularly when something isn't working as it should. However, customers shouldn't be made to feel as though they are the problem, particularly when they are simply trying to use the facility correctly and are actively requesting assistance.

I think management should be made aware of what happened and I would ask that the staff member's conduct be addressed. If there are particular requirements regarding crushed bottles or how containers should be loaded into the machine, these should also be clearly communicated to customers rather than the staff member becoming visibly frustrated with them.

I'm not looking to make a huge issue out of what happened, but I do think it's important that management knows about it, as the behaviour we experienced was certainly not what I would expect from a customer-facing service.

Extremely disappointed with how RSPCA NSW has handled my dog Tina’s case.

Tina underwent dental treatment and shortly afterwards developed a serious retrobulbar infection requiring specialist treatment at SASH, leaving me with more than $5000 in additional veterinary costs.

RSPCA NSW has declined to cover these costs. However, in their written response, they stated that Tina’s X-rays taken before the extraction showed diseased molars that could have been a source of infection extending into the retrobulbar space.

My question is simple: if this was identified on her X-rays and was a potential source of such a serious infection, why was I never informed?

What upsets me most is thinking about what could have happened if Tina wasn't insured and I couldn't afford emergency specialist care. She could have lost her sight simply because I may not have been able to afford the treatment she urgently needed. No pet owner should have to face that situation without being properly informed of a known clinical concern.

I am not claiming negligence has been proven. I am asking for transparency, accountability and a clear explanation of what happened to Tina.

The matter is still ongoing and I hope RSPCA NSW will reconsider their response.

one_star_reviews.text:
I wish I had sought a second opinion sooner.

IF YOU HAVE ENDOMETRIOSIS, PLEASE SEE AN ENDOMETRIOSIS SPECIALIST.

I had my first laparoscopy for endometriosis with Dr Ginni Mandapati in August 2024.

After that surgery, I was told my endometriosis had been “everywhere,” but that it had all been removed. I was given the understanding that there was no endometriosis left in my body.

Despite this, I became significantly worse after surgery.

When I repeatedly returned because I was still experiencing severe pain, I felt completely dismissed. I was told my pain was “in my head,” that I needed to “get over it” and “change my lifestyle.” At one point, my symptoms were blamed on alcohol despite the fact that I don’t drink.

I was also told to “come back in 10 years to get the Mirena out.”

I was left with no clear understanding of exactly what had been done during my surgery. To this day, I still have so many unanswered questions.

Eventually, I couldn’t accept that this level of pain was something I simply needed to “get over,” so I sought a second opinion.

Only around five months after being told that all of my endometriosis had been removed, I underwent another surgery with an endometriosis specialist.

Significant and extensive endometriosis was found throughout my pelvis and diaphragm , as well as disease involving areas outside the pelvis. I required extensive surgery.

My second surgery was so significant that I spent four days in the ICU afterwards.

It was incredibly difficult to process.

Only months earlier, I had been given the understanding that every bit of my endometriosis had been removed and that there was none left in my body. I had been told, essentially, that I needed to get over my pain.

Then, five months later, I was undergoing another major operation for extensive disease.

I was subsequently told that it would not have been possible for that amount of endometriosis to simply grow back in such a short period of time.

That left me with an incredibly painful question: if it couldn’t have grown back to that extent in five months, what had actually happened during my first surgery?

I also experienced problems with a Mirena inserted during my treatment. The strings had been cut so short that they were not accessible, and its eventual removal was extremely painful and distressing.

The consequences of everything that happened have been enormous.

I have lived with chronic pelvic pain, undergone two major surgeries within months of each other, required ongoing specialist pain management and long-term treatment, spent tens of thousands of dollars on medical care, and had my ability to work and live normally significantly affected.

I eventually made a formal complaint to the original clinic.

Following my complaint, I was offered a refund of money ….conditional on signing an agreement that included confidentiality provisions, not pursuing further complaints, ending the therapeutic relationship, and acknowledging that the clinic denied wrongdoing.

I did not sign it.

I can only speak about what happened to me and my own experience of the care I received, but it has had a profound impact on my life and my trust in medical care.

I wish I had listened to my body and sought another opinion much earlier.

If you are still experiencing significant symptoms after endometriosis surgery and feel that your concerns are being dismissed, please advocate for yourself and consider seeking a second opinion from an endometriosis specialist.

I am extremely grateful that I eventually did.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience as a client of iSupervise was unsatisfactory, mainly because of the organisation of visits, the transition process and communication.
Of eleven scheduled visits, five were cancelled, and the actual contact time I had was approximately six hours in total. During the visits that went ahead, transitions took between 40 and 60 minutes out of bookings lasting only two hours. In my experience, no transition took less than 40 minutes, significantly reducing the time available.
Throughout this process, I tried to contribute suggestions to make transitions shorter and more effective. I repeatedly asked for alternative arrangements to be considered to preserve the available contact time. Despite those requests, I did not see an improvement that brought transitions below those durations.
Communication was also frustrating. In my experience, phone calls went unanswered, leaving me dependent on email replies, which did not always arrive in time to clarify or resolve arrangements for a visit. I had to follow up repeatedly and encountered errors and inconsistencies in communications about times and locations.
On some occasions, I was told that changes were being considered, but I did not receive a clear and timely explanation of what had been proposed, what had been agreed and what would actually be implemented.
Prospective clients should also ask about the additional travel charge that may apply depending on the location of the visit.
I raised these concerns directly with the service. I am sharing my experience to document the difficulties I encountered and help others make an informed decision.
I recommend obtaining written clarification about how transitions are managed within the booked time, what happens when they take up a substantial part of a visit, cancellation and rescheduling conditions, additional travel charges and the complaints process.

We ordered glasses and contact lenses for our son from OPSM Belconnen on 31 July 2026. We were later sent a message advising that our order was ready for collection on 6 August.
We went to the store on 8 August to collect the order, only to be told that the glasses were ready but the contact lenses were not. We were told that we would be contacted once the lenses arrived.
We waited for about a week and a half and, as we had not received any update, my wife called the store to check on the order. We were then told that the contact lenses had actually not been ordered.
My wife asked if she could speak with Michelle, the optometrist who had dealt with us. We were told that Michelle was not at work and that she would call us on Friday when she returned.
We waited for almost another two weeks, but received no phone call or message.
Today, 29 August, my wife called OPSM Belconnen again to find out what was happening. To our surprise, we were once again told that the contact lenses had not been ordered. We were then told that they would order them today and hopefully we would receive them by next Friday.
This has been very disappointing and frustrating. We understand that mistakes can happen, but the lack of communication and the fact that we have had to repeatedly contact the store ourselves to find out what is happening is not the level of service we expected from OPSM.
I would like to ask the management team at OPSM Belconnen to please look into this matter and find out where the confusion occurred. If there was something we were required to do from our end that we had not completed, we would genuinely like to know so we can avoid this happening again in the future.
We chose OPSM expecting a professional and reliable service, particularly when it comes to something as important as our son's vision. We hope management can investigate what happened and provide us with some clarity and an explanation.

Thanks for nothing.

Anthony Stewart.

one_star_reviews.text:
Please don’t waste your money.

I had been a regular client at this clinic for almost a year, so what happened was extremely disappointing.

On one occasion, the owner called me the day before my appointment asking me to reschedule because the entire centre had a training day. I had actually taken a day off work for that appointment, but I was understanding because I know things happen and I was happy to accommodate them.

Later, I had a microneedling appointment booked, but shortly beforehand my skin had suddenly become very congested with active acne. After assessing my skin, I genuinely felt that microneedling was not the safest or most appropriate option at that time, so I contacted them to cancel. I understand that it was outside their cancellation policy, and I was prepared to discuss it reasonably given that I was a long-term, regular client.

What really shocked me was the response from the owner. I was told that I still needed to come in and have another treatment. When I asked what would happen if someone became seriously unwell or had an accident and couldn’t attend, I was told that even if someone had an accident, they would still be charged.

As a customer and simply as a human being, I found that response incredibly upsetting. I understand businesses need policies, but I also believe there should be compassion and reasonable exceptions, particularly when someone’s health and skin are involved.

The only reason I continued going there for as long as I did was because of Serveh, who was absolutely wonderful and provided the best service.

There are other providers offering the same treatments with much better customer service and, in my experience, a much more understanding approach. Please do your research and consider your options before spending your money here.

First of all: Our IVF cycle was ultimately successful thanks to our doctor, so this isn't about the clinical care — it's about how we were treated by administrative staff along the way.

Communication was inconsistent from the start. We were pushed to begin treatment almost immediately after being in talks with them, then handed a large amount of paperwork and told staff would walk us through each step as we reached it — that follow-through never really happened. We were also managing this from a remote location, so all our contact was by phone, and it felt like that made it easy for the clinic to lose track of us. There were logistical mistakes too, including wrong items and paperwork sent more than once.

When I raised these concerns on the phone, the staff member became defensive and ended the call. Shortly after, a senior administration officer called and told me she could cancel my upcoming procedure — despite my doctor being ready to proceed — unless I confirmed in writing that I'd received everything I needed and felt prepared. I was mid-cycle at the time and felt I had no real choice but to comply, even though it didn't reflect how I actually felt. That is not how any patient should be treated at one of the most vulnerable times in their life. I do therefore not recommend this place!

I would strongly NOT recommend Greg Watts Used Cars based on my experience.

I purchased a 2011 Mini Cooper from this dealership only TWO MONTHS AGO, and I am already dealing with multiple significant mechanical problems.

There was a noise coming from the rear of the car AT THE TIME I BOUGHT IT. I specifically questioned the dealer about this before purchasing the vehicle and was assured it was nothing to worry about. I relied on that assurance.

I have since had the car checked and was advised that the rear shocks require significant work, estimated at approximately $2,000.

On top of that, the air conditioning has stopped working and I am now experiencing problems with the gearbox.

I was also sold a warranty and was led to believe I would have protection if mechanical problems arose. Now that I actually need it, I am being told these problems are not covered.

I have contacted the dealer repeatedly and asked them to inspect the vehicle and help resolve these issues. I have not received a satisfactory resolution.

I even offered to sell the vehicle BACK TO THEM FOR LESS than I paid for it only two months ago just to put an end to this situation. They refused.

I am absolutely furious and extremely disappointed with my experience. I deliberately purchased from a car dealership rather than privately because I expected greater protection and peace of mind. Instead, within approximately two months I have a vehicle with multiple problems and potentially thousands of dollars in repairs.

I have given the dealer the opportunity to resolve this directly. As that has not happened, I am now taking the matter to NSW Fair Trading.

Anyone considering purchasing a vehicle here should, in my opinion, get a completely independent mechanical inspection BEFORE handing over any money and read every detail of the warranty rather than relying on what you are told.

This review reflects my personal experience with this dealership.

I am becoming Saul Bellow’s Herzog.

I’ll start off by saying I’ve never had a bad interaction with any staff members.

The problem seems to be dysfunctional systems that deluge staff preventing timely responses.
The issues with getting through on the phone are well documented, I’d get to the moon sooner.

Two incidents stand out:
-	There was an admin error that stopped me from receiving the Medicare rebate on three occasions. This was only resolved after repeated follow-ups from me and my psychiatrist. I emailed three times in three weeks and on the third occasion reluctantly indicated I’d escalate. After this, they processed my refunds within minutes.

-	They incorrectly booked a 15-minute telehealth consultation despite all previous appointments being booked for 30 minutes in person. My psychiatrist subsequently transferred. The booking issue was not resolved and ultimately resulted in the loss of a month of treatment.

I’m cool with errors, they happen, but there’s no getting around the consequences.

An error occurred, everyone agreed there was a problem, I copped the consequences, yet accountability seemed to evaporate at every step.

I have been receiving psychiatric care at Recentre for several years and, for the most part, have had very positive experiences with my psychiatrist, nursing staff and other administrative staff. I am genuinely grateful for the care I have received from many members of the team.

Unfortunately, my experiences with the admissions intake process have been consistently distressing. On multiple occasions, when I have been at my most unwell and have reached out for help, I have felt spoken to in a way that was dismissive, cold and made me feel as though I was a burden or an inconvenience.
I completely understand that admissions are not always possible, that bed availability can be limited, and that there are processes that need to be followed. I am not expecting preferential treatment or an immediate admission. What I do expect, however, is to be treated with compassion and respect when I am reaching out to a psychiatric hospital because I am struggling.
I have not required an admission for over a year, and it took a significant amount of courage for me to make the call today. I was understandably disappointed to learn that my psychiatrist is currently on leave, but I accepted that an admission may not be feasible under those circumstances and was willing to follow the appropriate alternative pathway. I called back because I felt I needed to communicate just how unwell and desperate I was feeling, and after explaining my circumstances, I left the conversation feeling completely dismissed.
This is particularly upsetting because I have been a patient of Recentre for years. I recognise that I have not always been the easiest patient to care for and that the symptoms of severe mental illness can be challenging. However, that should never mean that someone seeking help is made to feel as though they are unwanted or a burden.
I am now seriously considering changing psychiatrists and moving to another facility, which is incredibly disappointing given the positive relationship I have had with my treating psychiatrist and other members of the team.
I hope Recentre takes this feedback seriously. Admissions staff are often the first point of contact for people who are frightened, overwhelmed and potentially at their lowest point. The way someone is spoken to in that moment matters enormously. A little compassion, patience and understanding can make a profound difference.

People do not contact psychiatric hospitals because they are having a good day. They contact them because they need help. Please remember that behind every phone call is a person who is struggling.

A 10% discount does not change the fact that I paid for a product advertised as 125ml and received 100ml, a 20% difference in volume.

The owner also states that the listing was an error, yet the product had apparently been advertised as 125ml for months. Other Google reviews  confirm and also raise other concerns about similar issues. That makes this more concerning than what could simply be dismissed as a one-off typo.

I also remain concerned about the quality of the fragrance, as its scent disappears in less than an hour. The owner says the fragrances are authentic and sourced through authorised channels, but that does not address my experience and others with the product itself.

Most importantly, businesses need to get things right the first time. Customers today have plenty of choices and when they feel disappointed or misled, they often simply take their business elsewhere rather than giving a company a second chance. Customer trust is hard to earn and very easy to lose!

My experience has raised serious concerns about accuracy, transparency, value and customer service with this business. I recommend potential customers read the Google reviews carefully and make their own decision before purchasing.

⭐️ Very disappointing experience

There were 9 children in a Sunday morning swimming class with only one instructor.

After each child had only two opportunities to practise diving(it took more time than usual), all nine children were then split into three lanes, with three children in each lane being supervised by just one instructor. At that point, I honestly questioned whether this was really a swimming lesson or simply children being given a lane to swim in.

My child has been taking swimming lessons for more than five years, and I have never seen a class with more than five children until today.

Rackley Swimming’s own information describes its programs as having “small class sizes.” I would genuinely like to ask Rackley: Do you consider nine children with one instructor to be a small class?

I am extremely concerned about both the children’s safety and whether they are receiving proper and effective swimming instruction under these circumstances.

What is even more disappointing is that the class size was increased so significantly without any prior notice to parents.

I sincerely hope Rackley does not simply use the make-up class arrangement as an excuse for what happened. Whatever the reason, nine children being taught by one instructor deserves a proper explanation.

I would genuinely like to hear Rackley Swimming’s response and position on this situation.

For anyone considering swimming lessons at Rackley, I strongly recommend reading this review before enrolling. Children’s safety and quality swimming education should always come first.

one_star_reviews.text:
I attended this clinic for a relatively short period when I was exploring the possibility of having a baby on my own. At the time, I didn’t know what my natural fertility was like or whether I would have difficulty becoming pregnant, which was why I sought professional advice in the first place.

What I found particularly upsetting was the repeated emphasis on my age. I was made to feel that I was already too old to freeze my eggs and that IVF was essentially my only realistic chance of becoming a mother, using donor sperm. I left those appointments feeling devastated, hopeless and as though my opportunity to have a child had already passed me by.

I was also extremely disappointed to later discover that “polycystic follicular disease” had been documented in my medical history. This was never discussed with me or explained to me during my appointments, and I have subsequently been told that this diagnosis does not appear to be accurate. Unfortunately, it has followed me into my pregnancy records, and I now find myself having to explain or address it at midwifery appointments.

My experience ultimately turned out very differently from the picture that had been presented to me. At age 40, I became pregnant naturally and very easily.

I completely understand that fertility does decline with age and that healthcare professionals have a responsibility to discuss those statistics and potential risks with patients. However, there is an enormous difference between providing realistic, evidence-based information and making a woman feel that pregnancy after a certain age is virtually hopeless.

Women deserve balanced information about fertility, including the limitations of population statistics and the fact that individual fertility can vary considerably. Women over 35 should not automatically be made to feel that their chances of becoming mothers have disappeared.

The way fertility information is communicated matters. For someone who desperately wants a child, repeatedly being told that they are “too old” can be incredibly distressing. I hope greater consideration is given to how these conversations are handled in the future so that women receive honest information without unnecessarily having their hope taken away.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our experience with Dr Gavin Sacks and his team at IVF Australia was extremely disappointing, particularly given how significant, emotional and physically demanding the IVF process is for patients.

At the time of our treatment, Dr Gavin Sacks was in the final stages of transitioning away from IVF Australia. Unfortunately, we were not informed that he was about to leave and that we were among his last patients at IVF Australia. We believe this was important information that should have been communicated to us before proceeding with such a significant treatment.

From the beginning, we did not feel that Dr Sacks took enough time to properly listen to everything we had to say or fully understand our concerns and circumstances before starting the IVF cycle. We often felt that the process was rushed and that there was not enough attention given to our individual situation. We expected much more communication, patience and genuine consideration before making decisions that could have such a major impact on our lives.

IVF is not simply another medical procedure. For patients, it involves emotional preparation, physical challenges, financial commitment and incredibly important decisions about their future and family. We understand that for a busy fertility clinic, patients may become part of a routine process, but for us, this was not routine—it was one of the most important and difficult decisions of our lives. Unfortunately, we did not feel that this was reflected in the way we were treated.

Throughout the cycle, we found Dr Sacks to be insufficiently attentive and caring. We did not feel that he was listening to us properly or giving our concerns the attention they deserved. We expected to feel supported and confident in our treating doctor, but instead, we often felt like just another number going through the system.

What was particularly upsetting was what happened after the cycle was unsuccessful. Unfortunately, there was no follow-up or support at all from Dr Sacks or his team after the cycle failed. Given the emotional and physical impact of an unsuccessful IVF cycle, we expected some communication, guidance and support during such a difficult time. Instead, we were left feeling completely unsupported and on our own after the treatment.

Overall, we are very unhappy with the care and support we received from Dr Gavin Sacks and his team. We sincerely believe that fertility treatment requires not only medical knowledge and expertise, but also listening, empathy, communication and genuine care for the people behind the treatment.

Behind every IVF cycle is a person or couple placing enormous trust in their doctor and making deeply personal decisions about their future. Patients should never feel that they are simply a number in a process. For us, this was a life-changing decision, and unfortunately, we did not feel that our experience was treated with the level of care, attention and compassion that it deserved.

DO NOT USE STAR CITY REMOVALS.... I only wish I had of carefully scrutinised the significant amount of reviews across multiple platforms regarding this company - all with the same theme of complaints !!!

It was a nightmare from the start. It was an 3 bdrm interstate end of lease move for me and the removalist pick up date was a (Monday) 20 July. I received a text on from Star City on 18 July (Saturday) to inform there were delays with the truck and pick-up had been moved to 21 July. This caused a domino effect with all other services (i.e, cleaners, carpet cleaners, pest control, etc), none of which could be contacted over the weekend, and resulted in me having to pay an additional days rent, with other services having to access the property after the owner had moved back in. The owner also had to reschedule her removalist and services.

On the day of pick-up one of the drivers pulled me aside after they had packed 3/4 of the truck and told me my belongings exceeded the quote price. The original quote was for 34 m3 $3,990, he stated it was approximately 40m3 and he would need to contact logistics to send me a new quote and I would need to pay the balance same day.

Prior to the truck leaving, I had to do a tip run. I gave clear instructions on what needed to go and what needed to stay. When I returned, several items had been left behind, and items belonging to the property were taken. I had to replace these. After the truck left I received an email with a new quote for 42m3 ($5,498.00). Star City had my furniture and I had no other alternative than to pay. In addition to an extra 8m3, they also charged an additional 4 hours excess loading time.

The truck was a day late arriving. They were informed the drivers needed to reassemble the furniture they had taken apart during pick up, and my large hardwood desk needed to be taken upstairs. When I arrived at the property. One bed had be taken upstairs and reassembled, and the rest of my furniture had been dumped in the downstairs living area. The damage to my furniture is heartbreaking. My entire dining room suite and several other items are damaged beyond repair and evidence complete and utter negligence on the part of this company.

I have been sending emails and phoning the company, however, they simply ignore my requests or inform the person working in the "claims" area is off sick.

I have attached some photos of the damage to my dining room suite. However, there are many other pieces of furniture that have been damaged beyond repair. There was no option to provide zero star review, so I have had to provide a minimum 1 star in order to proceed with this review.

I am extremely dissatisfied with my experience dealing with CollectMORE, particularly my telephone dealings with Paul.
In my personal experience, I found the manner in which Paul communicated to be unnecessarily aggressive, confrontational and lacking the level of professionalism I would reasonably expect from an organisation operating in the debt-collection industry. The tone and approach adopted during our conversations added considerable and unnecessary stress to an already difficult financial situation.
I was also very concerned about the fees being charged, which I considered excessive. While I fully acknowledge that debt recovery is a legitimate commercial activity and that outstanding financial obligations must be addressed, this does not remove the need for communications to be conducted professionally, respectfully and with appropriate consideration of a person's circumstances.
What concerned me further was CollectMORE's public response to my original review. Rather than addressing my concerns in a constructive and professional manner, the response publicly characterised my conduct as "deplorable" and described my concerns regarding the fees as "bizarre". In my view, this response only reinforced my concerns regarding the manner in which complaints and disagreements are handled.
For the avoidance of doubt, this review reflects my personal experience and opinion arising from my direct dealings with CollectMORE. I believe consumers are entitled to express genuine concerns about the manner in which they are treated, including concerns regarding communication, fees and the handling of complaints.
Based solely on my experience, I would not recommend CollectMORE. I would strongly encourage management to review its communication practices and the manner in which legitimate customer concerns and public feedback are addressed.

I had a very poor experience dealing with Collectmore Debt Collection, particularly with Paul.
I found Paul’s manner on the phone extremely unprofessional, aggressive and unnecessarily demanding. The way he communicated made an already stressful financial situation significantly worse. In my experience, there was very little patience, understanding or compassion shown.
I was also extremely disappointed with the level of fees being charged. I found them very expensive, particularly considering that the person being pursued is already experiencing financial pressure. Rather than trying to communicate respectfully and work towards a reasonable solution, I felt the main focus was simply on extracting payment as urgently as possible.
I understand that debt collection is their business and that debts need to be addressed, but that does not mean people should be spoken to without dignity or understanding. There is a professional and respectful way to deal with people who are experiencing financial difficulties.
Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend Collectmore. I sincerely hope management reviews the way customers and debtors are communicated with, particularly over the phone.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience, particularly with the quality control and the way the situation was handled by the manager.

I was originally told my car would be ready on 03/09, but received a call on 29/08 saying it was already repaired and ready for collection. I took a day off work to collect it on 01/09 and returned my hire car.

Shortly after driving out, I noticed my  indicator flashing unusually fast and immediately drove back.

While staff were checking the car, I heard them discussing that the indicator was working now but “wasn’t working a few days ago.” This was extremely concerning because it suggested the issue had already been noticed before I collected the vehicle. If there was a known issue, why was the car released without confirming it had been resolved?

When I spoke to the manager, I was told that part of the repair had been done elsewhere and they did not know everything that had been done. From a customer’s perspective, this is not an acceptable explanation. If your repair centre is returning the vehicle to me as ready, it should be properly checked regardless of where the work was completed.

I was then told the repair could take another hour. The alternative was another hire car, which would take approximately two hours to arrange, or I could drive my car away and return the following day. None of these options addressed the fact that I should not have been asked to collect the vehicle before it was properly checked.

The manager also told me that the call asking me to collect the car had come from my insurer rather than the repair centre. I contacted my insurer myself and confirmed that the number that called me on 29/08 was in fact from the repair centre.

I was also repeatedly told that newer electric vehicles are still new and repairers are learning to work on them. If a vehicle is unfamiliar or technically complex, I would expect it to be checked more carefully before being returned to a customer.

While I was on the phone with my insurer trying to resolve the situation, the manager told me, “I’m trying to help, don’t be rude.”

I was frustrated because I had taken time off work, returned my hire car, travelled there after being told my vehicle was ready, discovered an issue immediately after leaving, and then had to contact my insurer myself to clarify conflicting information.

To be fair, the technician who worked on the car after I returned was helpful and ultimately resolved the issue, and I genuinely appreciate his assistance. My complaint is not directed at him.

The biggest issue was the quality control and management of the situation. Customers should not be the final quality-control check after driving a supposedly repaired vehicle out of a repair centre.

One star based on my experience with how this situation was managed.

one_star_reviews.text:
One of the worst customer service experiences I have ever had. Based on my experience, I would not recommend Westpoint Auto to anyone.

My finance application was rejected, so I requested the return of my $1,013 deposit. I sent an email requesting the refund on 25 August. During a phone call, I was told to “consider the worst-case scenario” and that I would receive my deposit back by 28 August.

However, on 29 August, I was told that the accounts team only processes refunds on Tuesdays and Thursdays. If that is the case, I don't understand why the refund wasn't processed on Thursday, 27 August. Then, Tuesday, 1 September also passed without receiving the refund.

Today, 3 September, I called again to follow up. I was told that the refund had been approved, but they couldn't confirm when I would actually receive the money.

I was also told by a salesperson that “big companies have standard procedures for handling accounts.” If this is their standard procedure, I have to seriously question how they handle their customers' money.

There is another issue that concerns me. When making the deposit, I was required to pay a surcharge, and I included the surcharge amount in my refund request. However, when the salesperson called me, I was told that they could guarantee the deposit would be refunded, but they could not guarantee the surcharge.

Is this really how a large company should handle customers' money? If I was required to pay the surcharge as part of the original transaction, I believe there should be clear communication about whether and why it is refundable, rather than leaving the customer uncertain after the finance application has been rejected.

For me, this isn't just about the $1,013 refund or the surcharge. It's about keeping your word, following through on commitments, and communicating honestly and clearly with customers. I was given multiple explanations and timeframes, yet the refund was still not received.

Unfortunately, this experience has completely damaged my trust in the company. I would strongly recommend considering another dealership, such as Von Bibra, rather than going through the same frustration I experienced with Westpoint Auto.

Very disappointing service, communication, and handling of customers' money. I would not recommend this dealership based on my experience.

I applied for a job several times with this employment agency in Brisbane. Recently, however, I had better luck and someone responded – they emailed me from their office. It was a woman named Nikhole . She presented me with an offer of training, which to me as a mature person, I should take advantage of. At the end, she wrote: "Would you be open to a quick chat to explore this further?" I thought the offer is sensible and logical. So I quickly replied. Days passed and nothing, no response. I replied again, and still no response. After a few days, I decided the best solution would be to contact this job agency and her by phone. Several times, a young man with a deep basy voice answered at the beginning, but he told me Nikhole is busy and is unable  talk to me, but she would call me back later. Nothing of the sort happened and probably never will.
But simply why she did not respond me , just write a few words or call back and say, "I'm sorry, but the training offer I promised you in email with the phone call is no longer valid."
Unfortunately, the younger generation lacks basic principles, empathy, and an understanding that others need work to pay their bills, mortgage that they need to change careers, and that stress will ensue. The time is money. For these people at employment agencies, the average person is just another number, just another number for which they need to get paid by their bosses. It's sad, but that's reality. Would I recommend such a "ghost" employment agency to reasonable thinking people? Answer this question for yourselves before signing any contract.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had my 2022 Mitsubishi ASX serviced at Lander Mitsubishi Prospect and unfortunately I was very disappointed with the experience.

Straight after the service, while I was still at the dealership, I noticed a new engine noise that had never been there before. I raised it immediately and was told it was normal for this model. I have owned the car since 2022 and know how it normally sounds, which is why I was concerned. I also asked for my concern and their findings to be provided in writing, but I was unable to obtain a proper written report at the time.

Another serious concern was the battery test carried out during the service. Lander’s report recorded my battery as a “Regular Flood Battery”, rated it at 355 CCA and gave a result of “REPLACE”.

The battery actually fitted to my car is clearly labelled as a Calcium Battery, 600 CCA (SAE). I subsequently had the same battery tested by NRMA using the correct battery specifications. Although the battery was only 45% charged at the time, NRMA’s test result was “GOOD & RECHARGE”, with 425 CCA measured. NRMA also checked the cranking voltage, alternator and parasitic drain, and all passed.

I find the difference between these two tests concerning. In particular, I would like Lander Mitsubishi to explain why a 600 CCA calcium battery was tested or recorded as a 355 CCA regular flooded battery before I was advised that it needed replacement. If a customer is being asked to approve and pay for a new battery, I think it is reasonable to expect the test to be carried out using the correct specifications for the battery actually installed in the vehicle.

Between the new engine noise immediately after the service, the difficulty obtaining proper written documentation at the time, and the discrepancy in the battery testing, I have lost confidence in the service I received.

I have now lodged a formal complaint with NSW Fair Trading regarding my concerns and have also arranged an independent inspection of the vehicle.

I am sharing my experience based on the service records and battery test reports I received, and I hope Lander Mitsubishi provides a proper explanation for what occurred.

one_star_reviews.text:
Bought my son a 3 x hot lap ticket from Adrenaline for his 13th birthday, when we arrived, there was still "drive laps" going on which was not a problem.  While watching the drive laps noticed a couple of cars doing full laps of what I later figured was apparently two tracks, used to go in opposite directions.  We had to wait for all other cars to finish so "both" tracks were clear, I assumed this was because the "hot laps" would be around the "whole track", which would make sense as the Adrenaline website describes the experience as "approximately 30 minutes in the car"! His first lap which I videoed, was 1 min 9 sec, the 2nd lap seemed a bit quicker, and the 3rd lap is cut short to leave the track to the staging area, would be generous to say he was in the car for 3 minutes (plus about 3 minutes strapping in and getting out). After a long drive out, during which he was really excited, then waiting for other drivers to finish, it was ultimately really disappointing and made us feel that we were the customer that just needed to be gotten out the way, because they were behind in the schedule.
Unfortunately, the viewing area was all taped off, not that it would really have been worth going up to.  The staff were friendly, but unfortunately the experience for him was not even close to what he had hoped for.

### Very disappointing communication and unresolved refund

I enrolled my two-year-old daughter on 1 June 2026 and paid $215. I arrived at the premises 10 minutes early, as requested, only to receive a call advising that the class had been cancelled because the trainer was unwell. I was told that the class fee would be credited.

On 10 June, I paid a further $244.95 for a costume and shoes recommended by the business. Unfortunately, my daughter was then injured and, on medical advice, was unable to attend any classes or collect the costume and shoes.

I contacted the business by text to explain the situation, cancel her enrolment, and ask about the discontinuation process and a refund for the uncollected costume and shoes. Jenny acknowledged my message on 27 June and advised on 30 June that she would discuss the refund with Ashleigh.

Since then, I have received no response, despite sending three follow-up messages. I have paid a total of $459.95, my daughter did not attend any classes, the costume and shoes were never collected, and I am still waiting for a clear response or resolution.

I understand that illness and unexpected circumstances can occur, but the ongoing lack of communication and failure to address a reasonable refund request have been extremely disappointing. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this business.

There are many elderly people who use this post office. If they aren’t tech savvy, or need help, I have no idea how they would get anything dealt with here given the staff.

I have been used to Black rock post office where Harry and his team are exemplary. I will continue to do all but pick up parcels there.

This is without doubt the worst post office I’ve encountered.
